## Do the models form the same groups?

Each model grouped its own arguments, so each came up with its own groups and its own names for them. The table shows the three sets side by side. Click on a row to read the full name and definition of a group.

```{r}
#| label: table-groups-all-models
#| code-summary: "Table of the argument groups of all three models"

model_labels <- c(gemini = "Gemini", openai = "GPT", anthropic = "Claude")

# All arguments with their groups, one row per argument and model.
df_arguments_grouped_all <- bind_rows(
  gemini = df_arguments_grouped_gemini,
  openai = df_arguments_grouped_openai,
  anthropic = df_arguments_grouped_anthropic,
  .id = "llm"
)

# Per model and group: number of submissions raising at least one argument of the group.
df_table_groups_all <- df_arguments_grouped_all %>%
  distinct(llm, submission_id, group_id, group_keyword, group_name, group_definition) %>%
  count(llm, group_id, group_keyword, group_name, group_definition, name = "n_submissions") %>%
  mutate(
    model = factor(model_labels[llm], levels = model_labels),
    percent = round(100 * n_submissions / nrow(df_corpus), 1)
  ) %>%
  mutate(is_top = n_submissions == max(n_submissions), .by = llm) %>%
  mutate(bar_colour = if_else(is_top, "firebrick", "grey65")) %>%
  arrange(model, group_id) %>%
  select(model, group_keyword, n_submissions, percent, group_name, group_definition, bar_colour, is_top)

reactable(
  df_table_groups_all,
  theme = compact_table_theme,
  fullWidth = TRUE,
  compact = TRUE,
  highlight = TRUE,
  outlined = TRUE,
  pagination = FALSE,
  columns = list(
    model = colDef(name = "Model", width = 80),
    group_keyword = colDef(name = "Group", minWidth = 180),
    n_submissions = colDef(name = "Submissions", width = 110, align = "right"),
    percent = colDef(
      name = "Share",
      minWidth = 120,
      cell = reactablefmtr::data_bars(
        df_table_groups_all,
        fill_color_ref = "bar_colour",
        text_position = "outside-end",
        number_fmt = \(x) str_c(x, "%"),
        max_value = 100
      )
    ),
    group_name = colDef(show = FALSE),
    group_definition = colDef(show = FALSE),
    bar_colour = colDef(show = FALSE),
    is_top = colDef(show = FALSE)
  ),
  # The full name and definition of a group open when its row is expanded.
  details = function(index) {
    htmltools::div(
      style = "padding: 4px 8px; font-size: 11px;",
      htmltools::tags$b(df_table_groups_all$group_name[index]),
      htmltools::tags$br(),
      df_table_groups_all$group_definition[index]
    )
  },
  rowStyle = function(index) {
    if (df_table_groups_all$is_top[index]) list(background = "#fde0dd", fontWeight = "bold")
  }
) %>%
  style_reactable_table(
    title = "ARGUMENT GROUPS OF THE THREE MODELS",
    subtitle = str_glue(
      "Share of the {nrow(df_corpus)} analysed submissions raising at least one argument of the group; largest group of each model highlighted"
    )
  )
```

Names alone do not show whether two groups hold the same arguments. The links between arguments do: for every pair of linked arguments, I look up the group which each of the two models chose. If two models group alike, the arguments of one group of the first model end up in one and the same group of the second. Each graph below compares two models. A row is a group of the first model, a column a group of the second, and each cell gives the number of linked pairs.

```{r}
#| label: group-crosstab-definition
#| code-summary: "Compare the groups of two models through linked arguments"

# Linked pairs of arguments with the group which each model chose.
df_argument_groups <- df_arguments_grouped_all %>%
  select(llm, submission_id, argument_nr, group_id, group_keyword)

df_links_grouped <- df_argument_links %>%
  left_join(df_argument_groups, by = join_by(llm_a == llm, submission_id, argument_nr_a == argument_nr)) %>%
  left_join(df_argument_groups, by = join_by(llm_b == llm, submission_id, argument_nr_b == argument_nr), suffix = c("_a", "_b"))

# Heatmap of the groups of one model (rows) against those of another (columns).
plot_group_crosstab <- function(llm_row, llm_col) {
  df_crosstab <- df_links_grouped %>%
    filter(llm_a == llm_row, llm_b == llm_col) %>%
    count(group_id_a, group_keyword_a, group_id_b, group_keyword_b, name = "n_pairs") %>%
    mutate(share_of_row = n_pairs / sum(n_pairs), .by = group_id_a) %>%
    mutate(
      group_keyword_a = fct_rev(fct_reorder(group_keyword_a, as.integer(factor(group_id_a)))),
      group_keyword_b = fct_reorder(group_keyword_b, as.integer(factor(group_id_b)))
    )

  ggplot(df_crosstab, aes(x = group_keyword_b, y = group_keyword_a, fill = share_of_row)) +
    geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 1) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = format(n_pairs, big.mark = ",", trim = TRUE), colour = share_of_row > 0.6),
      family = "Noto Sans", size = 3
    ) +
    scale_fill_gradient(low = "grey95", high = "firebrick", limits = c(0, 1), guide = "none") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "grey20", `TRUE` = "white"), guide = "none") +
    scale_x_discrete(position = "top", labels = \(x) str_wrap(x, 12)) +
    labs(
      title = str_wrap(str_glue("Do {model_labels[[llm_row]]} and {model_labels[[llm_col]]} form the same groups?"), 70),
      subtitle = str_glue(
        "Linked pairs of arguments by the group of {model_labels[[llm_row]]} (rows) and of {model_labels[[llm_col]]} (columns). ",
        "Colour: share of the row, from 0% (grey) to 100% (red)."
      ),
      x = NULL,
      y = NULL,
      caption = attribution_graph()
    ) +
    theme_post() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}
```

::: {.panel-tabset}

One number sums up each comparison: the share of linked pairs which fall into the best-matching group of the other model. If the groups of one model were simply renamed groups of the other, it would be 100%.

```{r}
#| label: group-agreement-table
#| code-summary: "Share of linked pairs in the best-matching group of the other model"

df_links_grouped %>%
  count(llm_a, llm_b, group_id_a, group_id_b, name = "n_pairs") %>%
  summarise(n_best = max(n_pairs), n_pairs = sum(n_pairs), .by = c(llm_a, llm_b, group_id_a)) %>%
  summarise(n_pairs = sum(n_pairs), share = sum(n_best) / sum(n_pairs), .by = c(llm_a, llm_b)) %>%
  transmute(
    `Groups of` = model_labels[llm_a],
    `Compared with` = model_labels[llm_b],
    `Linked pairs` = n_pairs,
    `In best-matching group` = str_c(format(round(100 * share, 1), nsmall = 1), "%")
  ) %>%
  kable_attributed(align = "llrr", format.args = list(big.mark = ","))
```
